steps.title: Enthalpy per unit volume
steps.why: Energy is stored in the ice, the air and the vapor. With pressure work and kinetic energy left out, the stored energy is enthalpy, so the energy per unit total volume is the sum over the phases.
steps.operation: sum of phase enthalpies weighted by mass per unit volume

check.printed: Definition. It cannot be checked by a tool.

steps.title: Energy conservation
steps.why: For a fixed control volume, $E$ changes only by the energy flux through its surface. The flux is Fourier conduction plus the enthalpy carried by diffusing vapor. The ice is fixed in place and the air is at rest.
steps.operation: conservation law in local form (divergence theorem on an arbitrary control volume)

check.printed: Statement of the conservation principle. It cannot be checked by a tool.

steps.title: Water mass conservation
steps.why: Total water (ice plus vapor) is conserved, and only vapor moves. This balance links the vapor flux divergence to the change in ice fraction, which brings in the phase change.

check.printed: Statement of the conservation principle. It cannot be checked by a tool.

steps.title: Expand and use the mass balance
steps.why: Apply the product and chain rules to $\partial_t E$ and $\nabla\cdot(h_v\mathbf{j}_v)$, with $\partial_t m_a = 0$. The terms multiplying $h_v$ are $h_v$ times the left side of S3 minus $\rho_i\partial_t\phi$, so they combine with $\rho_i h_i\partial_t\phi$ into $-\rho_i(h_v-h_i)\partial_t\phi$.
steps.operation: product rule, chain rule $\partial_t h(T)=c\,\partial_t T$, substitution of S3

steps.title: Drop vapor enthalpy advection
steps.why: The term $c_v\mathbf{j}_v\cdot\nabla T$ is heat carried by the vapor flux. Compared with conduction it scales as $|\mathbf{j}_v| c_v \ell/k \approx 2\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m^{-1}}\cdot\ell \sim 10^{-11}$ for a pore scale $\ell\sim10^{-4}$ m, so it is dropped.
steps.operation: neglect a term of relative order $|\mathbf{j}_v|c_v\ell/k$

steps.title: Residual in Cartesian coordinates
steps.why: Write the divergence in $x,y,z$ and move every term to one side. Every term has units of W m$^{-3}$. Sublimation ($\partial_t\phi<0$) cools the material, as it should.
steps.operation: expand $\nabla\cdot$ in Cartesian coordinates and collect terms in $R$

assumptions_used: A1: $\phi$ is a known, smooth field (given).
A2: Pressure work, viscous heating, and kinetic energy are negligible, so the stored energy is the enthalpy.
A3: The ice density $\rho_i$ is constant (rigid ice, no thermal expansion). This step needs it so that $\rho_i\phi$ is the ice mass per unit volume and $\partial_t(\rho_i\phi)=\rho_i\partial_t\phi$.
A4: The ice is fixed and the gas has no bulk flow. Only water vapor moves, by diffusion with flux $\mathbf{j}_v$. The air mass per unit volume $m_a$ is constant in time.
A5: Heat is conducted by Fourier's law with an effective conductivity $k(\phi,T)$. Thermal radiation across pores is folded into $k$ or neglected.
A6: Ice and gas share one local temperature $T$ (local thermal equilibrium), and the vapor flux is small (see S5).

neglected.effect: Enthalpy carried by vapor diffusion, $c_v\mathbf{j}_v\cdot\nabla T$
neglected.why: Its ratio to conduction is about $10^{-11}$ at pore scale for $\rho_v\sim10^{-7}$ kg m$^{-3}$ near 200 K (check_size).

neglected.effect: Pressure work and kinetic energy of the gas
neglected.why: The gas is at rest and at very low pressure. $Dp/Dt$ work is of order $\rho_v$ times the vapor heat content, which is far below $\rho_i c_i \partial_t T$.

neglected.effect: Advection by bulk gas flow, and air mass change as pores open (if $m_a$ is not constant)
neglected.why: $m_a\ll\rho_i$ (lunar pore gas is near vacuum), so any $h_a\partial_t m_a$ term is smaller than the latent term by $m_a h_a/(\rho_i L)\lesssim10^{-6}$.
The relative density change is about $10^{-4}$ per K times $\Delta T$, which is small over the temperature range.

neglected.effect: Interface (surface) energy and curvature (Gibbs-Thomson) contribution to the energy
neglected.why: The surface energy per unit volume, $\gamma/\ell\sim0.1/10^{-4}=10^3$ J m$^{-3}$, is far below the latent heat $\rho_i L\sim2.6\times10^9$ J m$^{-3}$.

At about 200 K, radiative conductance $4\epsilon\sigma T^3\ell\sim2\times10^{-4}$ W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ for $\ell=10^{-4}$ m. This is far below $k$ of ice ($\sim2$). It can be included in $k$ if needed.
